chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Fī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Bakīr, from Zurārah, from Abū ‘Abd Allāh (peace be upon him), who said:
Verily, there was a king of great status who was in his own gathering; he began to discuss the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, and then he disappeared, and it is not known what became of him.
ai.seo_question: What happened to the king who discussed the Essence of God?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this narrative illustrates the principle of *al-hudud* (divine boundaries), warning that excessive speculation (*ta'til*) regarding Allah’s Essence (*Dhat*) can lead to spiritual disorientation or loss. It serves as a foundational text in Shia theology for distinguishing between knowing God’s attributes and attempting to comprehend His unknowable essence, a theme central to the works of al-Sharif al-Murtada and al-Tusi.
